summary.headline: Aarti Industries Q1 FY27 revenue rose 41% YoY to Rs 2,627 crore and EBITDA 79% to Rs 385 crore, with management refusing to guarantee the run rate.
summary.overview: Revenue of Rs 2,627 crore (+41% YoY) and EBITDA of Rs 385 crore (+79% YoY) were lifted by raw-material price pass-through, product mix, and inventory and FX gains, which management sized at roughly Rs 50-60 crore. Volumes fell sequentially (energy -17% QoQ, non-energy -7%, overall about -12%) amid West Asia disruption and high raw-material prices. Zone IV commissioning is delayed by 3-6 months due to labour shortages, and management declined to commit to a forward EBITDA run rate. The Augene JV is near commissioning, and FY27 capex remains on track at Rs 700-800 crore.

segments.name: Energy (Fuel Additives)
segments.commentary: Fuel additives capacity expanded to 360 KTPA from 290 KTPA; West Asia share fell to about 2% from about 15%, and volumes were redirected to US, Africa, Europe and India. Gasoline-naphtha cracks averaged about $15-18/bbl, and management expects the capacity to reach high utilisation in Q1 itself.

segments.name: Non-Energy - Polymers
segments.commentary: Demand was soft in Q1 on weak downstream US and China demand, and low shipments followed heavy Q4 FY26 bulk shipments to the US. Management expects recovery in Q2 and full-year growth.

segments.name: Non-Energy - Dyes & Pigments
segments.commentary: Demand remained subdued amid high raw-material prices and seasonality. Price increases in dyes and pigments and pharma were partly linked to China's VAT removal on the NCB chain.

segments.name: Non-Energy - Pharma and Agro
segments.commentary: Pharma demand was stable. Agrochemical volumes were marginally lower as customers resisted elevated raw-material-linked prices; recovery is expected in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY28 EBITDA target of Rs 1,800 crore retained; the Augene JV is included in this guidance, but management said Zone IV ramp-up may be slower than originally assumed.
Management declined to guide to a sustainable quarterly EBITDA run rate, citing plus/minus 15-20% monthly price volatility; it expects volume growth to offset lost inventory gains.
Augene JV (50:50, consolidated at PAT level) expected to start operations in Q2 FY27, with steady-state revenue retained at Rs 300-400 crore.
FY27 capex on track at Rs 700-800 crore; capex intensity expected to fall significantly from FY28.

Zone IV commissioning is delayed 3-6 months; the MPP is expected to produce first product in August 2026 and commissioning will be announced thereafter. Management expects 5-10 products in FY27 and 25-30 by FY28.
Sabic-linked backward-integration project commissioning expected around Sep-Oct 2027.
capex_capacity: Fuel additives capacity expanded to 360 KTPA from 290 KTPA; management said there is no fixed limit on further expansion, and it will first demonstrate utilisation over the next 12 months.
Zone IV: 97% of equipment erected and 85% of piping complete across the five chemistry blocks; full manpower restored, with commissioning expected in FY27 and ramp-up over FY28-FY29.
PEDA project in market seeding and expected to commercialise soon; DCB debottlenecking to 140 KTPA under evaluation.
NCB chain debottlenecking is being evaluated within existing assets given demand in India.
Aarti Circularity plastic recycling plant with Re Sustainability slated for commissioning in H2 FY27.
demand_pricing: Raw-material inflation (benzene, sulphur, methanol, aniline) was passed through to customers; high prices reduced purchasing power in dyes, selected agro and polymer compounds.
Gasoline-naphtha cracks averaged $15-18/bbl, which management described as healthy, while the energy business remains volatile.
Exports were 59% of revenue; US-bound DAP shipments carry 2-3 month voyage times that delay revenue recognition.
China's suspension of export tax rebates is creating opportunities for the NCB value chain.
Non-energy volumes fell on delayed purchasing in a high-price environment, with some supply-chain effects; management said Middle East exposure in non-energy is low.

qa_highlights.question: What were the FX and inventory gains in Q1, and what is the impact on the EBITDA base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated a Rs 50-60 crore impact but said it is hard to quantify because of intra-quarter volatility; the CFO said FX gains came from squaring off import positions as the rupee moved in a Rs 92-97 range, and management advised treating this as operating profit with no forward commitment.

qa_highlights.question: Why was gross margin lower sequentially despite the inventory and FX benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly gross margin is not a reliable steady-state indicator, citing timing of raw-material purchases and product placement, freight, lower volumes raising operating costs, and the chemical business running on absolute rupee deltas rather than percentage margins.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Zone IV delay affect FY28 EBITDA visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the MPP and calcium chloride unit are on track, but the five chemistry blocks face slower ramp-up than originally planned, and it will share ramp-up details once the blocks commission.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Augene JV affect reported EBITDA, and is it in the Rs 1,800 crore guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed that the Rs 1,800 crore FY28 guidance includes Augene EBITDA, while the Re Aarti JV is not expected to contribute meaningfully before FY28; reporting treatment for JVs is yet to be finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Is the energy business's volume, capacity and market share sustainable once West Asia normalises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business remains in a market-development phase; the portfolio is diversified across US, Africa, Europe, Middle East and India (Southeast Asia not yet penetrated), and it expects utilisation gains rather than volume shifts when West Asia reopens.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the company stop disclosing absolute sales volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it removed absolute sales numbers from slides because they were being used in an unfavourable way, and now gives energy/non-energy volume growth plus value-chain utilisation ranges.

risks_watch: Zone IV: five chemistry blocks face a 3-6 month delay and slower ramp-up; the MPP first product is expected in August 2026, and the FY28 Rs 1,800 crore EBITDA guidance (which includes Augene) depends on this ramp-up.

Earnings quality: management said FX and inventory gains (Rs 50-60 crore, roughly Rs 47 crore per an analyst's figure) helped Q1, and it declined to commit to a forward quarterly EBITDA run rate given plus/minus 15-20% monthly price swings.

Energy seasonality and West Asia: management expects winter weakness from late October to December, and West Asia volumes (share down to about 2% from about 15%) are not yet restored; utilisation of the 360 KTPA fuel additives capacity is the key test over the next 12 months.
Working capital and leverage: management said working capital expanded and debt and finance costs rose in Q1; watch debt levels as imported-raw-material inventory (1-1.5 months) carries price risk.

Augene JV commissioning in Q2 FY27 and the Re Aarti JV reporting treatment, which management has yet to finalise; watch the Rs 300-400 crore steady-state revenue assumption and PAT-level consolidation.

summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, volume recovery and capacity, but cautious and evasive on earnings visibility: management repeatedly declined to quantify forward EBITDA, gross margin or inventory/FX gains, citing volatility. Candid about Zone IV execution delays and the West Asia impact on energy volumes.
